structured.answer: According to the page, the cheapest is an account at פסגות with the fund "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125". With 10,000 now and 500 a month, I'd put in 70,000 and have about 86,045 ₪ after ten years. At the big banks it would be about 81,000–83,000. I'm not acting on it myself; I'll ask my son first, because of the minus signs and the words I don't understand.

stuck.why: "להשקיע במדד": to me מדד is the price index from the news, and the buttons are full of English letters (MSCI, S&P 500). I nearly left.
"−1,030 ₪ לעומת הבחירה שלכם" with a minus sign. I backed away from that option without really understanding it.
"−0.04% בשנה · שנה אחת" has a minus on the fund marked as the choice. I didn't know whether it means it lost money, and it worried me.
The colour key is only at the bottom, after all the rows. I had to go back up to match colours to bars, and the oranges and yellows look alike.

findings.what: Minus sign on the recommended fund (−0.04%) with no explanation scares me away from the very fund the page recommends
The opening speaks of מדד and English index names; nothing says on the first screen whether this is safe or risky
Every bank row repeats 'לא בחישוב מחיר אחר לצעירים, לחיילים...' so I reread the same words on each row to find what's different
Colour key for the bars is far below the bars; I have to look back and forth, and the orange and yellow are close
Small grey numbers and dotted underlines; I don't know what the second number in each row is
Dark background with grey text is hard to read even enlarged
Unknown company names (אינטראקטיב, אלטשולר טרייד, מיטב טרייד, אקסלנס) I wouldn't trust
